When you were talking about how the shape creates a "sauce trough," I thought at first that this wasn't a particularly appealing feature to me, since I like a very scant amount of sauce on my pasta. But then I thought about how rotini is often my go-to pasta shape, and all the good nooks and crannies it has, and ... maybe sauce retention is MORE important for people who like just a little sauce on their pasta. Because you gotta get that little bit of sauce to really stick and coat the pasta all over. And the texture variance aspect is obviously very appealing to me - what I like about rotini is how tender the outside of the spiral is and how firm the middle stays, and the cascatelli looks like it would have WAY more variation than the rotini. Like the places where the I-beam-like shape happens... SQUISH. Can't believe I'm about to get on a waitlist for a pasta.

In Italian the word for 'waterfall' is 'cascata' and the diminutive form is 'cascatella'. The plural form of nouns ending in -a is -e so it should actually be 'cascatelle' not 'cascatelli'. 'cascatelli' would be the plural of the nonexistent word *'cascatello' (nouns ending in -o are pluralised with -i), which would be the diminutive form of *'cascato' which would be some sort of masculine waterfall. Maybe that's what they were going for?
Note: yes, there are some rare exceptions to the pluralisation rule
